message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"remedio","gloss":"remedy","category":"remedy/medicine","note":"The word is followed by 'contra la dificultad de aprender y retener' (remedy against the difficulty of learning and retaining). So it is a remedy against a difficulty, not a pharmakon 'of memory and wisdom'. The translator adds a footnote marker {33}."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"retener","gloss":"to retain","note":"The genitive μνήμης is turned into an infinitive, 'retener', inside 'dificultad de aprender y retener'. The word 'memoria' appears only in the preceding clause, 'servirá a su memoria', which renders μνημονικωτέρους."},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"aprender","gloss":"to learn","note":"σοφίας becomes the infinitive 'aprender' (learning). 'más sabios' (wiser) in the preceding clause renders σοφωτέρους, not this genitive."},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"medio","gloss":"means, way","category":"means/aid","note":"The phrase is 'un medio de cultivar la memoria' (a means of cultivating memory). It is not the same word as the earlier 'remedio'. Elsewhere Thamus's 'auxilio extraño' (foreign aid) renders the writing-trust clause, not pharmakon."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"la memoria","gloss":"the memory","note":"Thamus says 'cultivar la memoria' (to cultivate memory). The negation 'not of memory but of reminding' is recast as 'not a means of cultivating memory, but of awakening reminiscences'."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"reminiscencias","gloss":"reminiscences, recollections","note":"The phrase is 'despertar reminiscencias' (to awaken reminiscences). The Greek noun for the act of reminding becomes a plural noun of things recalled."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"la sombra de la ciencia","gloss":"the shadow of knowledge/science","note":"δόξαν (seeming) becomes 'sombra' (shadow). σοφία becomes 'ciencia' (science, knowledge). It continues 'y no la ciencia misma' (and not knowledge itself), so the doxa/aletheia contrast is carried by shadow versus the thing itself."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"falsos sabios","gloss":"false wise men","note":"The compound is split into adjective plus noun. 'Falsos' (false) replaces the sense of seeming-wise. The clause 'instead of wise' (ἀντὶ σοφῶν) is dropped."},"argument":"Azcárate gives Theuth 'remedio' and Thamus 'medio'. The Greek word is not repeated, so Thamus does not turn Theuth's own word against him. Theuth's cure is also reshaped into a remedy 'against the difficulty of learning and retaining'. Thamus's reply therefore reads as a quiet correction of what the invention is for ('a means of cultivating memory, not of awakening reminiscences'), and the ambivalence of pharmakon, as cure and poison, disappears."}
message.reasoning:
I'm checking how the Spanish translation handles the pharmakon passage—looking at how "remedio" is used for the difficulty of learning and retaining, and tracing whether "memoria" captures mneme's nuance in that key clause.

Now I'm comparing 275a, where pharmakon shifts to "un medio," distinguishing cultivating memory from awakening reminiscences, and noting "la sombra de la ciencia" for sophia and "falsos sabios" for doxosophoi. The shift from "remedio" to "medio" loses the pun Thamus plays on Theuth's original word, which seems like a key point to flag.
